record.paper_title: A generalization of the Collatz problem and conjecture
record.context_brief: Counterexample search in unbroken parameter regimes
record.original_question: For integers b >= 2 and m >= 1, define the generalized Collatz iteration on a positive integer x by replacing x with x/b when x is divisible by b and replacing x with (b^m + 1)x + b^m - (x mod b^m) when x is not divisible by b. Call the starting values of the form S0 = s b^N with s < b^m and N >= 0 trivial, since these are already covered by the proved convergence result. In the parameter regimes m = 1 with b equal to 5, 7, or 8; m = 2 with b > 2; and m > 2 with b >= 2, can one find starting values outside that trivial family whose trajectories do not reach the Collatz-type cycle 1, 2b^m, 2b^(m-1), ..., 2b, 2, 3b^m, 3b^(m-1), ..., 3b, 3, ..., b - 1, ..., b, 1, for example by entering a different finite limit cycle or by diverging?

evidence.quote: Define the function f(n, b, m) as follows (n, m = 1, 2, ..; b = 2, 3, ...): f(n, b, m) = n/b if n ≡ 0 (mod b) , (3) f(n, b, m) = (bm + 1)n + bm − (n mod bm ) if n 6= 0 (mod b) .(4)

Of course this set can be trivially extended to an infinite set considering all the values S0 = s bN , s < bm, N = 0, 1, 2, .. For all these initial values the sequence (5) obviously converges to the number 1 and thus the limit cycle (17) due to the above Proposition and to the rule (3).
Let us call ’trivial’ all these values of S0 (and ”non-trivial ” the values outside this set).

Many other counter-examples can be found for m = 1; note however that we found none not only for b = 2 (this was expected since that is the original Collatz map) but also for other small values of b as b = 5, b = 7, b = 8 (and this was quite unexpected).
To our surprise, for m = 2, b > 2 and for m > 2, b ≥ 2 we have found no other counter-example...

we do not dare to propose a new general conjecture of the Collatz type (however we dare to offer C= 1 for each of the first 100 counter-examples in the cases m = 1, b = 5, 7, 8; m = 2, b > 2; m > 2, b >= 2 ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $b\ge 2$ and $m\ge 1$. Define a map $f_{b,m}:\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ by
$$f_{b,m}(n)=\begin{cases}n/b,& n\equiv 0\pmod b,\\ (b^m+1)\,n + b^m - (n\bmod b^m),& n\not\equiv 0\pmod b,\end{cases}$$
where $n\bmod b^m$ denotes the least nonnegative residue of $n$ modulo $b^m$. For a starting value $S_0\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, consider the orbit $S_0,\,f_{b,m}(S_0),\,f_{b,m}^2(S_0),\dots$.

It is known that the finite cycle
$$1,\,2b^m,\,2b^{m-1},\dots,2b,\,2,\,3b^m,\,3b^{m-1},\dots,3b,\,3,\,\dots,\,(b-1)b^m,\dots,(b-1)b,\,b-1,\,\dots,\,b,\,1$$
attracts every starting value of the form $S_0 = s\,b^N$ with $1\le s< b^m$ and $N\ge 0$; call such starting values trivial.

In each of the parameter regimes
- $m=1$ and $b\in\{5,7,8\}$,
- $m=2$ and $b>2$,
- $m>2$ and $b\ge 2$,

does there exist a non-trivial starting value $S_0\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ whose orbit under $f_{b,m}$ either fails to reach the above cycle by eventually entering a different finite limit cycle, or diverges to infinity?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work specifically resolving the existence of non-trivial divergent orbits or alternative limit cycles for this particular $(b^m+1)$-style generalization in the listed parameter regimes. General results on generalized Collatz maps establish lower bounds on cycle lengths and verify convergence up to large heights, but do not appear to settle the specific question. The status is therefore not verifiable from public sources.

status_evidence.title: On Cycles of Generalized Collatz Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies generalized Collatz Fk functions and their cycle structure but does not address the specific (b^m+1) family.
status_evidence.claim: Related generalized Collatz cycle results exist but do not resolve this particular family.

status_evidence.title: There are no Collatz-m-Cycles with m<=91
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds on cycle lengths for the standard Collatz problem.
status_evidence.claim: Cycle existence results for related Collatz generalizations remain partial.
